summary: Hike-in site in Payette NF: 1932 L-4 ground cabin replaced in 1966 by an R-6 flat-top cab on a 10-foot base; staffed in summer; NHLR-registered 2020.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

visit.trail_note: Hike-in per Idaho Fire Lookouts; a 2024 McCall Life feature describes a hike that climbs 1,600 feet

events.note: Earliest entry on Idaho Fire Lookouts known staff list
Replaced by a Region 6 flat-top (R-6) cab on a 10-foot block base
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 29, 2020

evidence.quote: IDAHO COUNTY HERSHEY POINT Payette National Forest

evidence.supports: first cabin L-4 ground cabin circa 1932
evidence.quote: Hershey Point Lookout first construction was a Region 1/L-4 design ground cabin built circa 1932.
Developed about 1932 with an L-4 cab, the present live-in flat cab atop a 10' concrete base, built in 1966, is staffed in the summer.

evidence.supports: 1966 Region 6 flat top cabin on 10 foot block tower
evidence.quote: A new structure was built in 1966, a Region 6 Flat Top cabin design on a 10 foot block tower.

evidence.supports: 1966 replaced with R-6 on 10 foot block tower
administered by US Forest Service, Payette NF
evidence.quote: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
hiked 1,600 feet up to Hershey Point

corrections.proposed: R-6 flat top (current cab); L-4 was the original 1932 cabin
corrections.why: NHLR says the 1966 structure is a Region 6 Flat Top cabin, and Idaho Fire Lookouts says it was replaced with R-6. L-4 describes only the first 1932 cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts say the 1966 cab sits on a 10-foot block tower. firelookout.com says a 10-foot concrete base. Both describe the same 10-foot base, so the story gives the height and notes the wording difference.
NHLR gives 8,232 ft (2,509 m) and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 8232 feet. The record's 2509.1 m matches.

notes_for_editor: The record's design L-4 applies only to the 1932 cabin; the current cab is R-6 (correction proposed). The record's kind two_story with height_m 3.0 is left as is: sources describe a 10-foot base under a flat-top cab, so the kind label may need a look. Access level is not set: the only signals are the Hike-In tag and the McCall Life hike description, with no closure or permit information found. The McCall Life feature centers on one staff member's personal experience; the story uses only lookout facts and names no one. Known-staff names on Idaho Fire Lookouts are omitted on purpose.
